description: ICS techniques mitigated by Execution Prevention, ATT&CK mitigation M0938 (v1.1)
name: Execution Prevention (M0938)

techniques.comment: Execution prevention may block malicious software from accessing protected resources through the command-line interface.

Use application control/allowlisting to restrict PowerShell hosts, script paths, interpreters, and child-process behavior to approved engineering and operational workflows. Prefer explicit allowlists over broad blocking on production OT systems.

Restrict cmd.exe, batch files, and command-shell child processes to approved binaries, paths, parent processes, accounts, and maintenance workflows on Windows-based ICS assets. Preserve documented vendor and engineering dependencies.

Restrict interactive and scripted shell execution on Linux, network, and embedded ICS assets to approved accounts, management paths, commands, and vendor workflows. Where full application control is unavailable, constrain SSH/Telnet access and privileged shell use to dedicated administration paths.
Use application control and macro/script restrictions to prevent unapproved VBS/VBA/VBScript execution, while explicitly allowlisting required vendor macros and engineering automation.

Restrict Python execution to approved interpreters, scripts, libraries, accounts, and paths. On engineering systems where Python is required, use positive allowlisting rather than disabling the interpreter.
Use application control to restrict wscript.exe, cscript.exe, mshta.exe, Node.js, and other JavaScript runtimes to approved paths, parent processes, scripts, and users.
Minimize the exposure of API calls that allow the execution of code.
Use tools that restrict program execution via application control by attributes other than file name for common system and application utilities.
Minimize the exposure of API calls that allow the execution of code.

Disallow the execution of applications/programs which are not required for normal system functions, including any specific command-line arguments which may allow the execution of proxy commands or application binaries.
Application control may be able to prevent the running of executables masquerading as other files.
